questions.learningObjective: Part count in a second case
questions.stem: A character is built from several component parts rather than a single element. How is such a character classified?

options.misconception: Confuses a single component with the whole character
Claims the character has only one part
Introduces the unrelated notion of a variant

questions.explanation: A character made from more than one component is described as a multi-part character, so option C is correct. Option A mistakes a component for the whole character, B asserts the opposite of the stated structure, and D introduces the unrelated idea of a variant form.

questions.topic: Two characters built from the same sound component

options.misconception: Assumes the sound part fixes the radical

questions.explanation: A shared sound component signals that the characters have similar pronunciation, so option D is correct. It does not guarantee the same radical (A), the same meaning (B), or the same stroke count (C); those properties are independent of the phonetic element.

questions.topic: What a sound-and-meaning compound lets you predict
questions.stem: A character combines a sound-bearing part with a meaning-bearing part. What does such a sound-meaning compound suggest to a reader?

options.misconception: Expects the compound to predict stroke count
Expects an exact rather than broad meaning

questions.explanation: In a sound-meaning compound the phonetic part hints at pronunciation while the semantic part hints at the broad meaning, so option B is correct. Option A expects an exact stroke count, C expects a fully precise meaning that the semantic part only approximates, and D concerns typeface rather than structure.

questions.topic: Codes that record a character's structure
questions.learningObjective: Structural codes in a second case
questions.stem: A scholar wants an input method that encodes a character by analysing the shapes at its corners. Which system fits?

options.misconception: Confuses a typeface label with an encoding method
Mistakes a tally for a structural code
Confuses dictionary lookup with corner analysis

questions.explanation: The four-corner code derives a numeric input from corner shapes, so option D is the system described. A font name (A) is a typeface label, a stroke count (B) is a simple tally, and a radical name (C) is a dictionary classification; none of them encodes corner structure.
questions.hint: Name the code built from a character's four corners.
